٦٧٠٤ — عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( سبعة يظلهم اللّٰه يوم القيامة في ظله يومَ لا ظلَّ إلا ظله: إمام عادل، وشاب نشأ في عبادة الله، ورجل ذكر اللّٰه في خلاء، ففاضت عيناه، ورجل قلبه معلق في المسجد، ورجلان تحابا في الله، ورجل دعته امرأة ذات منصب وجمالٍ إلى نفسها، قال: إني أخاف الله، ورجل تصدق بصدقة فأخفاها حتى لا تعلم شماله ما صنعت يمينه ).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٨٠٦)، ومسلم (١٠٣١:٩١).

6704 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “There are seven whom Allah will shade in His Shade on the Day of Resurrection when there is no shade except His Shade: a just ruler; a youth who grew up in the worship of Allah; a man who remembered Allah in private and his eyes overflowed with tears; a man whose heart is attached to the mosque; two men who love each other for the sake of Allah; a man whom a woman of position and beauty invited to herself, and he said, 'Indeed, I fear Allah'; and a man who gave charity and hid it so that his left hand did not know what his right hand had spent.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6806) and Muslim (1031:91).

٦٧٠٥ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إن المقسطين عند اللّٰه على منابر من نور، عن يمين الرحمن عز وجل، وكلتا يديه يمينٌ، الذين يعدلون في حكمهم وأهليهم وما ولوا)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٧).

6705 — 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, the just will be with Allah on thrones of light, at the right hand of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Sublime—and both of His hands are right hands—those who are just in their ruling, with their families, and in what they have been placed in charge of.”
Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1827).

٦٧٠٦ — عن عياض بن حمار المجاشعي أن نبي اللّٰه ﷺ قال ذات يوم في خطبته فذكر الحديث: قال: (( أهل الجنة ثلاثة: ذو سلطان مقسط متصدق موفق، ورجل رحيم رقيق القلب لكل ذي قربى ومسلم، وعفيف متعفف ذو عيال... )) فذكر الحديث.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٨٦٥).

6706 — 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i narrated that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said one day in his sermon, and he mentioned the hadith: He said: “The people of Paradise are three types: a person of authority who is just, gives charity, and is guided to success; a merciful man who is soft-hearted to every relative and Muslim; and a chaste man who refrains from begging despite having a family...” and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.
Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (2865).

٦٧٠٧ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( ثلاثة لا ترد دعوتهم: الإمام العادل، والصائم حتى يُفطر، ودعوة المظلوم تحمل على الغمام، وتُفتح لها أبوابُ السماء، ويقول الرب: وعزتي لأنصرنك ولو بعد حين )).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٥٩٨)، وابن ماجه (١٧٥٢)، وأبوداود الطيالسي (٢٧٠٧) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٣٤٢٨).

6707 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There are three whose supplication is not rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the oppressed person, which is raised above the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for it, and the Lord says: 'By My Might, I will surely grant you victory, even if it is after some time.'”
Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3598), Ibn Majah (1752), and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (2707), and graded authentic (Sahih) by Ibn Hibban (3428).

٦٧٠٨ — عن أبي أيوب قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( يد اللّه مع القاضي حين يقضي، ويد اللّٰه مع القاسم حين يَقسم ).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٥١١). وقوله: ((يد اللّه مع القاضي)): يعني إذا قضى بالعدل.

6708 — Abu Ayyub said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The hand of Allah is with the judge when he judges, and the hand of Allah is with the distributor when he distributes.”
Hasan: Narrated by Ahmad (23511). His saying, “The hand of Allah is with the judge,” means when he judges with justice.

٦٧٠٩ — عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( لا حسدَ إلا في اثنتين: رجلٌ آتاه الله مالاً، فسلّطه على هلكته في الحق، وآخر آتاه اللّٰه حكمةً فهو يقضي بها ويعلِّمها )).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧١٤١)، ومسلم (٨١٦).
قال الحافظ: "وفي الحديث الترغيب في ولاية القضاء لمن استجمع شروطه، وقوي على أعمال الحق، ووجد له أعوانا لما فيه من الأمر بالمعروف ونصر المظلوم، وأداء الحق لمستحقه وكف يد الظالم والإصلاح بين الناس، وكل ذلك من القربات، ولذلك تولاه الأنبياء ومن بعدهم من الخلفاء الراشدين، ومن ثمّ اتفقوا على أنه من فروض الكفاية؛ لأن أمر الناس لا يستقيم بدونه". الفتح (١٢١/١٣).

6709 — Ibn Mas'ud said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and empowered him to spend it entirely in the cause of truth, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom and he judges by it and teaches it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7141) and Muslim (816).
Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said: “In this hadith, there is an encouragement to assume the position of judgeship for whoever meets its conditions, is strong enough to implement the truth, and finds helpers for it, because it involves enjoining what is right, assisting the oppressed, delivering rights to those entitled to them, restraining the hand of the oppressor, and making peace between people. All of these are acts of drawing near to Allah. For this reason, it was undertaken by the Prophets and after them by the Rightly Guided Caliphs. Hence, they agreed that it is a communal obligation (Fard Kifayah), because the affairs of people cannot be set straight without it.” Fath al-Bari (13/121).

٦٧١٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: لعن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ الراشي والمرتشي في الحكم.
حسن: رواه الترمذي (١٣٣٦)، وأحمد (٩٠٢٣)، وابن الجارود (٥٨٥) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٥٠٧٦).
وقوله: (( الراشي)) وهو المعطي، و(( المرتشي)) وهو الآخذ، وإنما يلحقهما العقوبة معا إذا استويا في القصد والإرادة، فرشا المعطي لينال به باطلا، ويتوصل به إلى ظلم، وأما إذا أعطى ليتوصل به إلى حق، أو يدفع عن نفسه ظلما فإنه غير داخل في هذا الوعيد" ذكره الخطابي.

6712 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who offers a bribe and the one who takes it in judgment.
Hasan: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1336), Ahmad (9023), and Ibn al-Jarud (585), and authenticated (Sahih) by Ibn Hibban (5076).
His saying: “'al-Rashi' (the briber) is the giver, and 'al-Murtashi' (the bribed) is the taker. The punishment only applies to both of them together when they are equal in intent and will, meaning the giver offers the bribe to obtain something false or to commit an injustice. However, if he gives it to reach a right or to fend off an injustice from himself, then he is not included in this threat.” This was mentioned by al-Khattabi.

6714 — 'Amr ibn al-'As narrated that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “If a judge passes judgment having striven to reach the correct decision (ijtihad) and is correct, he will have a double reward; and if he passes judgment having striven to reach the correct decision and makes a mistake, he will have a single reward.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Chapter of Adherence to the Book and Sunnah (7352) and Muslim in the Chapter of Judgments (1716:15).

٦٧١٦ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( القضاة ثلاثة، واحد في الجنة، واثنان في النار: فأما الذي في الجنة فرجل عرف الحق فقضى به، ورجل عرف الحق فجار في الحكم فهو في النار، ورجل قضى للناس على جهل فهو في النار)).
حسن: رواه أبوداود (٣٥٧٣)، وابن ماجه (٢٣١٥)، والطحاوي في مشكله (٥٥)، والبيهقي (١١٦/١٠).

6716 — Buraydah ibn al-Husayb narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Judges are of three types: one will be in Paradise and two in the Fire. As for the one in Paradise, he is a man who knew the truth and judged according to it. A man who knew the truth but acted unjustly in his judgment will be in the Fire. And a man who judged for the people out of ignorance will be in the Fire.”
Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3573), Ibn Majah (2315), al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar (55), and al-Bayhaqi (10/116).

٦٧١٧ — عن عبد الرحمن بن سمرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ: (( يا عبد الرحمن بن سمرة لا تسأل الإمارة، فإنك إن أوتيتها عن مسألة وكلت إليها، وإن أوتيتها من غير مسألة أعنت عليها)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٦٢٢) ومسلم (١٦٥٢).

Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6622) and Muslim (1652).

٦٧١٨ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إذا أراد اللّه بالأمير خيراً جعل له وزير صدق، إن نسي ذكّره، وإن ذكر أعانه، وإذا أراد اللّٰه به غير ذلك جعل له وزير سوء، إن نسي لم يذكّره، وإن ذكر لم يُعنه ).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٣٢) واللفظ له، والنسائي (٤٢٠٤) وأحمد (٢٤٤١٤) وابن حبان (٤٤٩٤).

6718 — 'Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If Allah intends good for a leader, He appoints for him a truthful minister (advisor); if he forgets, he reminds him, and if he remembers, he helps him. But if Allah intends otherwise for him, He appoints for him an evil minister; if he forgets, he does not remind him, and if he remembers, he does not help him.”
Sahih: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2932) and the wording is his, al-Nasa'i (4204), Ahmad (24414), and Ibn Hibban (4494).

٦٧١٩ — عن عائشة أنها قالت: كان عتبة بن أبي وقاص، عهد إلى أخيه سعد بن أبي وقاص، أن ابن وليدة زمعة مني، فاقبضه إليك، قالت: فلما كان عام الفتح أخذه سعد. وقال: ابن أخي، قد كان عهد إلي فيه، فقام إليه عبد بن زمعة فقال: أخي، وابن وليدة أبي، ولد على فراشه، فتساوقا إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال سعد: يا رسول الله ﷺ! ابن أخي، قد كان عهد إليّ فيه، وقال عبد بن زمعة: أخي، وابن وليدة أبي، ولد على فراشه، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( هو لك يا عبد بن زمعة )) ثم قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر )) ثم قال لسودة بنت زمعة: (( احتجبي منه )) لما رأى من شبهه بعتبة ابن أبي وقاص. قالت: فما رآها حتى لقي اللّٰه عز وجل.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٠) والبخاري (٧١٨٢) ومسلم (٣٦:١٤٥٧).

6719 — 'Aishah said: 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas entrusted his brother, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, saying, “The son of the slave-girl of Zam'ah is my son, so take custody of him.” She said: In the year of the Conquest (of Makkah), Sa'd took him and said, “He is my nephew; my brother entrusted him to me.” 'Abd ibn Zam'ah stood up and said, “He is my brother and the son of my father's slave-girl, born on his bed.” They both rushed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Sa'd said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! He is my nephew; my brother entrusted him to me.” And 'Abd ibn Zam'ah said, “He is my brother and the son of my father's slave-girl, born on his bed.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “He is for you, O 'Abd ibn Zam'ah.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “The child belongs to the bed (marriage), and for the adulterer is the stone.” Then he said to Sawdah bint Zam'ah, “Observe hijab before him,” due to the resemblance he saw in him to 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. She said: He never saw her until he met Allah, the Mighty and Sublime.
Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (20), al-Bukhari (7182), and Muslim (1457:36).

٦٧١٩ — عن عائشة أنها قالت: كان عتبة بن أبي وقاص، عهد إلى أخيه سعد بن أبي وقاص، أن ابن وليدة زمعة مني، فاقبضه إليك، قالت: فلما كان عام الفتح أخذه سعد. وقال: ابن أخي، قد كان عهد إلي فيه، فقام إليه عبد بن زمعة فقال: أخي، وابن وليدة أبي، ولد على فراشه، فتساوقا إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال سعد: يا رسول الله ﷺ! ابن أخي، قد كان عهد إليّ فيه، وقال عبد بن زمعة: أخي، وابن وليدة أبي، ولد على فراشه، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( هو لك يا عبد بن زمعة )) ثم قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر )) ثم قال لسودة بنت زمعة: (( احتجبي منه )) لما رأى من شبهه بعتبة ابن أبي وقاص. قالت: فما رآها حتى لقي اللّٰه عز وجل.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٢٠) والبخاري (٧١٨٢) ومسلم (٣٦:١٤٥٧).
6719 — 'Aishah said: 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas entrusted his brother, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, saying, “The son of the slave-girl of Zam'ah is my son, so take custody of him.” She said: In the year of the Conquest (of Makkah), Sa'd took him and said, “He is my nephew; my brother entrusted him to me.” 'Abd ibn Zam'ah stood up and said, “He is my brother and the son of my father's slave-girl, born on his bed.” They both rushed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Sa'd said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! He is my nephew; my brother entrusted him to me.” And 'Abd ibn Zam'ah said, “He is my brother and the son of my father's slave-girl, born on his bed.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “He is for you, O 'Abd ibn Zam'ah.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “The child belongs to the bed (marriage), and for the adulterer is the stone.” Then he said to Sawdah bint Zam'ah, “Observe hijab before him,” due to the resemblance he saw in him to 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. She said: He never saw her until he met Allah, the Mighty and Sublime.
Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (20), al-Bukhari (7182), and Muslim (1457:36).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (١) والبخاري (٧١٦٩) ومسلم (٤:١٧١٣).

٦٧٢١ — عن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ سمع خصومة بباب حجرته، فخرج إليهم فقال: (( إنما أنا بشر، وإنه يأتيني الخصم، فلعلّ بعضكم أن يكون أبلغ من بعض، فأحسب أنه صادق فأقضي له بذلك، فمن قضيت له بحق مسلم، فإنما هي قطعة من النار، فليأخذها أو ليتركها )).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧١٨١)، ومسلم (٥:١٧١٣).

6721 — Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a dispute at the door of his room, so he came out to them and said: “I am only a human being, and disputants come to me. Perhaps some of you are more eloquent than others, so I think he is truthful and judge in his favor accordingly. Therefore, if I judge in anyone's favor concerning the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7181) and Muslim (1713:5).

٦٧٢٢ — عن أم سلمة قالت: جاء رجلان من الأنصار إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يختصمان في مواريث بينهما قد درست، ليس بينهما بينة، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( إنكم تختصمون إلي، وإنما أنا بشر، ولعل بعضكم أن يكون ألحن بحجته من بعض، وإنما أقضي بينكم على نحو ما أسمع منكم، فمن قضيت له من أخيه شيئا فلا يأخذه، فإنما أقطع له قطعة من النار، يأتي به إسطاما في عنقه يوم القيامة ))، قال: فبكى الرجلان،
وقال كل واحد منهما: حقي لأخي، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أما إذ فعلتما هذا، فاذهبا فاقتسما وتوخيا الحق، ثم استهما، ثم يتحلل كل واحد منكما صاحبه )).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٥٨٤،٣٥٨٥) وأحمد (٢٦٧١٧) والدارقطني (٢٣٨/٤-٢٣٩) والحاكم (٩٥/٤).

6722 — Umm Salamah said: Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputing over old inheritance shares between them that had worn away, and they had no proof. The Prophet ﷺ said: “You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps some of you are more eloquent in presenting their argument than others, and I only judge between you based on what I hear from you. Therefore, if I judge in anyone's favor concerning something belonging to his brother, he must not take it, for I am only cutting out for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring as a yoke around his neck on the Day of Resurrection.” She said: The two men wept, and each of them said, “My right is for my brother.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Since you have done this, go and divide it, seek what is right, then draw lots, and let each of you declare the other free of blame.”
Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3584, 3585), Ahmad (26717), al-Daraqutni (4/238-239), and al-Hakim (4/95).

٦٧٢٣ — عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: (( كانت امرأتان معهما ابناهما، جاء الذئب، فذهب بابن إحداهما، فقالت لصاحبتها: إنما ذهب بابنك، وقالت الأخرى: إنما ذهب بابنك، فتحاكما إلى داود عليه السلام، فقضى به للكبرى، فخرجتا على سليمان بن داود عليهما السلام، فأخبرتاه، فقال: ائتوني بالسّكين أشقه بينهما، فقالت الصغرى: لا تفعلْ يرحمك اللّٰه هو ابنها، فقضى به للصغرى)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٧٦٩)، ومسلم (١٧٢٠).

6723 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There were two women who had their two sons with them. A wolf came and took away the son of one of them. She said to her companion, 'It took your son!' The other said, 'No, it took your son!' So they took their case to David (peace be upon him), and he judged in favor of the elder woman. They left and went to Solomon, the son of David (peace be upon them both), and informed him. He said, 'Bring me a knife so I may cut him in half between the two of you.' The younger woman said, 'Do not do that, may Allah have mercy on you! It is her son.' So he judged in favor of the younger woman.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6769) and Muslim (1720).
Ibn al-Jawzi said: “Solomon deduced the truth when he saw the matter was ambiguous, and he did excellently. Both of them judged by independent reasoning (ijtihad), because if David had judged based on a direct textual revelation, it would not have been permissible for Solomon to judge contrary to it.” Fath al-Bari (6/465).

٦٧٢٤ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إنما أنا بشر، ولعل بعضكم أن يكون ألحن بحجته من بعض، فمن قطعت له من حق أخيه قطعة فإنما أقطع له قطعة من النار)).
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٣١٨) وأحمد (٨٣٩٤) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٥٠٧١).

6724 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I am only a human being, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in presenting their argument than others. Therefore, if I cut off a piece from the right of his brother for him, I am only cutting out for him a piece of the Fire.”
Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (2318) and Ahmad (8394), and authenticated (Sahih) by Ibn Hibban (5071).

٦٧٢٥ — عن أبي ذر قال: قلت: يا رسول الله ﷺ! ألا تستعملني؟ قال: فضرب بيده على منكبي ثم قال: (( يا أبا ذر إنك ضعيف، وإنها أمانة، وإنها يوم القيامة خزي وندامة إلا من أخذها بحقها، وأدى الذي عليه فيها)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٥).

6725 — Abu Dharr said: I said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! Will you not appoint me to a position of authority?” He tapped my shoulder with his hand and then said: “O Abu Dharr, you are weak, and it is a trust, and on the Day of Resurrection it will be a cause of disgrace and regret, except for the one who takes it rightfully and fulfills the duty imposed upon him therein.”
Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1825).

٦٧٢٦ — عن أبي ذر أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: (( يا أبا ذر إني أراك ضعيفا، وإني أحب لك ما أحب لنفسي، لا تأمرنّ على اثنين، ولا تُولينّ مال يتيم)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٦). قال النووي: "هذا الحديث أصل عظيم في اجتناب الولايات، لا سيما لمن كان فيه ضعف عن القيام بوظائف تلك الولاية. وأما الخزي والندامة فهو في حق من لم يكن أهلاً لها، أو كان أهلاً ولم يعدل فيها، فيخزيه اللّه تعالى يوم القيامة ويفضحه، ويندم على ما فرّط. وأما من كان أهلا للولاية، وعدل فيها فله فضل عظيم، تظاهرت به الأحاديث الصحيحة " انتهى.

6726 — Abu Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Abu Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself: do not rule over even two people, and do not manage the property of an orphan.”
Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1826). Al-Nawawi said: “This hadith is a great foundational principle for avoiding public offices, especially for one who is weak in carrying out the duties of that position. As for the disgrace and regret, it applies to whoever is not qualified for it, or was qualified but failed to act with justice; Allah the Exalted will disgrace and expose him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will regret what he neglected. However, whoever is qualified for leadership and acts with justice will have an immense virtue, as supported by numerous authentic hadiths.” End quote.

٦٧٢٧ — عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( الناس كالإبل المائة لا يجد الرجل فيها راحلة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٤٩٨) ومسلم (٢٥٤٧).
قال البيهقي (١٣٥/١٠): "هذا الحديث قد يتأول على أن الناس في أحكام الدين سواء، لا فضل فيها لشريف على مشروف، ولا لرفيع منهم على وضيع، كالإبل المائة، لا تكون فيها راحلة، وهي الذلول التي ترحل وتركب، وجاءت فاعلة بمعنى مفعولة". وقيل: معناه أن الناس كثير، والمرضيُّ منهم قليل قاله ابن بطال أي الذين يتحملون عن الناس، ويكشفون كربهم وهم قليلون.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٤٩٨) ومسلم (٢٥٤٧).

english_source:
6727 — Ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “People are like a hundred camels; a man can hardly find a single riding camel among them.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6498) and Muslim (2547).
Al-Bayhaqi said (10/135): “This hadith may be interpreted to mean that people are equal in the rulings of religion; there is no preference therein for a person of noble status over a common person, nor for an elevated person over a lowly one, just like a hundred camels in which there is no riding camel—which is the submissive camel that is saddled and ridden, and the active participle 'raahilah' here functions as a passive participle meaning ridden. And it was said: its meaning is that people are many, but those who are pleasing among them are few, as stated by Ibn Battal, meaning those who carry the burdens of people and relieve their distress are few.”

٦٧٢٨ — عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة قال: كتب أبو بكرة إلى ابنه - وكان بسجستان - بأن لا تقضي بين اثنين وأنت غضبان، فإني سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: (( لا يقضين حَكَمٌ بين اثنين وهو غضبان)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧١٥٨)، ومسلم (١٧١٧:١٦).

6728 — 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah said: Abu Bakrah wrote to his son—who was in Sijistan—instructing him not to judge between two people while being angry, saying, “For I heard the Prophet ﷺ saying: 'A judge must not pass judgment between two people while he is angry.'”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7158) and Muslim (1717:16).

٦٧٢٩ — عن أم سلمة زوج النبي ﷺ عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال: (( إذا ابتلي أحدكم بالقضاء بين المسلمين فلا يقضين وهو غضبان، فليسوّ بينهم بالنظر والمجلس والإشارة، ولا يرفع صوته على أحد الخصمين)).
حسن: رواه الدارقطني (٢٠٥/٤) والبيهقي (١٣٥/١٠) وأبو يعلى (٥٨٦٧) وإسحاق بن راهويه (١٨٤٦).

6729 — Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If one of you is tested with judging between Muslims, he must not judge while he is angry, and he must treat them equally in his gaze, his seating arrangement, and his gesturing, and he must not raise his voice against one of the two disputants.”
Hasan: Narrated by al-Daraqutni (4/205), al-Bayhaqi (10/135), Abu Ya'la (5867), and Ishaq ibn Rahwayh (1846).

٦٧٣٠ — عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: بعثني رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى اليمن قاضياً. فقلت: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ترسلني، وأنا حديث السن، ولا علم لي بالقضاء؟ فقال: (( إن اللّٰه عز وجل سيهدي قلبك، ويثبّت لسانك، فإذا جلس بين يديك الخصمان فلا تقضين حتى تسمع من الآخر كما سمعت من الأول. فإنه أحرى أن يتبين لك القضاء )) قال: فما زلت قاضياً، أو ما شككت في قضاء بعد.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٥٨٢) واللفظ له، والترمذي (١٣٣١) والبيهقي (١٣٧/١٠).

english_source:
6730 — 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen as a judge. I said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! You are sending me while I am young in age and have no knowledge of judging?” He said: “Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Sublime will guide your heart and make your tongue firm. When the two disputants sit before you, do not judge until you hear from the second one just as you heard from the first. For that is more likely to make the correct judgment clear to you.” 'Ali said: After that, I never ceased to be a judge, or I never doubted a judgment since.
Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3582) and the wording is his, al-Tirmidhi (1331), and al-Bayhaqi (10/137).

٦٧٣١ — عن أبي هريرة وزيد بن خالد الجهني، أنهما أخبراه أن رجلين اختصما إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال أحدهما: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ اقض بيننا بكتاب الله. وقال الآخر، وهو أفقههما: أجل يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فاقض بيننا بكتاب الله. وائذن لي أن أتكلم قال: (( تكلم)) فقال: إن ابني كان عسيفا على هذا فزنى بامرأته. فأخبرني أن على ابني الرجم. فافتديت منه بمائة شاة وبجارية لي. ثم إني سألت أهل العلم فأخبروني: أن ما على ابني جلدُ مائة، وتغريب عام. وأخبروني أنما الرجم على امرأته. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أما والذي نفسي بيده، لأقضين بينكما بكتاب الله. أما غنمك وجاريتك فرد عليك )) وجلد ابنه مائة. وغرّبه عاماً. وأمر أنيساً الأسلمي أن يأتي امرأة الآخر. فإن اعترفت، رجمها، فاعترفت فرجمها.
متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٦) والبخاري (٦٦٣٣،٦٦٣٤) ومسلم (١٦٩٧،١٦٩٨).

متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٦) والبخاري (٦٦٣٣،٦٦٣٤) ومسلم (١٦٩٧،١٦٩٨).

6731 — Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani narrated that they informed him that two men brought a dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! Judge between us according to the Book of Allah.” The other, who was the wiser of the two, said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, judge between us according to the Book of Allah, and permit me to speak.” He said, “Speak.” The man said, “My son was hired as a laborer by this man and he committed adultery with his wife. I was told that my son was to be stoned to death, so I ransomed him with one hundred sheep and a slave-girl of mine. Afterward, I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that my son is only to receive one hundred lashes and a year of exile, and they informed me that stoning is only for his wife.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will surely judge between you according to the Book of Allah. As for your sheep and your slave-girl, they are to be returned to you.” Then he ordered his son to be lashed one hundred times and exiled for a year. He then commanded Unays al-Aslami to go to the wife of the other man, and if she confessed, to stone her. She confessed, so he stoned her.
Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (6), al-Bukhari (6633, 6634), and Muslim (1697, 1698).

٦٧٣٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( اللهم إني أحرّج حق الضعيفين: اليتيم والمرأة)). وفي رواية: (( مال الضعيفين)).
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٣٦٧٨) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٥٥٦٥) والحاكم (١٢٨/٤ ،٦٣/١) وأحمد (٩٦٦٦).
وقوله: ((أحرج حق الضعيفين)) أي أحرم مالهما على من ظلمهما.

6732 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, I declare inviolable the right of the two weak ones: the orphan and the woman.” And in another narration: “the property of the two weak ones.”
Hasan: Narrated by Ibn Majah (3678), and authenticated (Sahih) by Ibn Hibban (5565), al-Hakim (4/128, 1/63), and Ahmad (9666).
His saying: “'Uharriju' (I declare inviolable) the right of the two weak ones” means: I make their wealth forbidden to whoever oppresses them.

٦٧٣٣ — عن شريح بن هانئ، عن أبيه، أنه لما وفد إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وسمعه وهم يكنون هانئا أبا الحكم. فدعاه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال له: (( إن اللّٰه هو الحكم، وإليه الحكم، فلم تكنى أبا الحكم؟ )) قال: إن قومي إذا اختلفوا في شيء أتوني فحكمت بينهم، فرضي كلا الطرفين. قال: (( ما أحسن من هذا، فمالك من الولد؟)). قال: لي شريح، وعبدالله، ومسلم، قال: (( فمن أكبرهم؟)) قال: شريح، قال: (( فأنت أبو شريح)) فدعا له ولولده.
صحيح: رواه النسائي (٥٣٨٧). قد ثبت التحكيم في شأن الزوجين، وجزاء الصيد، وتحكيم سعد في قضية بني قريظة.
والتحكيم جائز غير لازم، وإنما هو فتوى للطرفين إذا شاؤوا أخذوا به، وإن لم يشاؤوا لجأوا إلى السلطان.

english_source:
6733 — Shurayh ibn Hani narrated on the authority of his father that when he came as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ heard them calling Hani by the kunyah (honorific nickname) 'Abu al-Hakam'. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and said to him, “Indeed, Allah is the Judge (al-Hakam), and to Him belongs all judgment, so why are you called Abu al-Hakam?” He said, “When my people dispute over something, they come to me and I judge between them, and both parties are pleased.” He said, “How excellent this is! What do you have of children?” He replied, “I have Shurayh, 'Abdullah, and Muslim.” He said, “Who is the eldest of them?” He replied, “Shurayh.” He said, “Then you are Abu Shurayh,” and he supplicated for him and his children.
Sahih: Narrated by al-Nasa'i (5387). Arbitration has been established in the matter of spouses (in marital discord), the compensation for hunting (while in Ihram), and the arbitration of Sa'd in the case of Banu Qurayzah.
Arbitration is permissible but not legally binding; rather, it is like a legal advisory for both parties—if they wish, they may accept it, and if they do not wish, they may resort to the ruler (ruling authority).

6734 — Wa'il ibn Hujr said: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a man came leading another man with a leather strap and said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! This man killed my brother.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Did you kill him?” He replied, “Yes, I killed him.” He asked, “How did you kill him?” He replied, “He and I were hitting a tree to shake down its leaves, then he insulted me and made me angry, so I struck him with the axe on his temple and killed him.” The Prophet ﷺ said to him, “Do you have anything to pay as blood money for yourself?” He replied, “I have nothing except my cloak and my axe.” He asked, “Do you think your people will ransom you?” He replied, “I am of less value to my people than that.” So the Prophet ﷺ threw his strap to the claimant and said, “Take your companion.” The man went away with him. When he turned back, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “If he kills him, he will be just like him.” The man returned and said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! It has reached me that you said, 'If he kills him, he will be just like him,' yet I took him by your command.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Do you not want him to bear your sin and the sin of your companion (brother)?” He said, “O Prophet of Allah, yes indeed.” He said, “Then let it be so.” The man then threw away the strap and let him go his way.
Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (1680). His saying: “'nis'ah'” refers to a rope made of leather strips. His saying: “'natakhabat'” means: we were gathering 'khabt', which is tree leaves. His saying: “'If he kills him, he will be just like him'” means: neither of them will hold any virtue or favor over the other because he has fully exacted his right from him—unlike the case if he were to pardon him, for then he would have the virtue, favor, immense reward in the Hereafter, and beautiful praise in this world.

٦٧٣٥ — عن ابن عباس قال: كان زوج بريرة عبداً يقال له: مُغيث، كأني أنظر إليه يطوف خلفها يبكي، ودموعه تسيل على لحيته. فقال النبي ﷺ لعباس: (( يا عباس ألا تعجب من حب مغيث لبريرة، ومن بغض بريرة مغيثاً ))، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( لو راجعتِه )) قالت: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ تأمرني؟ قال: (( إنما أنا أشفع )) قالت: لا حاجة لي فيه.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٥٢٨٣).

6735 — Ibn 'Abbas said: The husband of Barirah was a slave called Mughith. It is as if I can see him walking behind her, weeping, with his tears flowing down his beard. The Prophet ﷺ said to 'Abbas, “O 'Abbas, are you not amazed by Mughith's love for Barirah and Barirah's hatred for Mughith?” Then the Prophet ﷺ said to her, “If only you would go back to him.” She said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, are you commanding me?” He said, “I am only interceding.” She said, “I have no need for him.”
Sahih: Narrated by al-Bukhari (5283).

٦٧٣٦ — عن ابن عمر قال: سمعت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقول: (( من حالت شفاعته دون حد من حدود اللّه فهو مضاد لله في أمره)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٥٩٧) وأحمد (٥٣٨٥) والحاكم (٢٧/٢) وجاء فيه: (( ومن مات وعليه دين فليس بالدينار ولا بالدرهم ولكنها الحسنات والسيئات. ومن خاصم في باطل وهو يعلمه لم يزل في سخط اللّٰه حتى ينزع، ومن قال في مؤمن ما ليس فيه أسكنه اللّٰه ردغة الخبال حتى يخرج مما قال)).
وقوله: "من حالت شفاعته" : أي من ثبت في حقه حد من حدود الله، وبلغ ذلك إلى السلطان، وأما قبل البلوغ إلى السلطان أو ما كان من حق الآدميين فللحاكم أن يشفع، بل يستحب له ذلك ولو ببذل المال، كما كان النبي ﷺ يفعل. قيل لعلي، وقد شفع لسارق: أتشفع لسارق؟ فقال: نعم، إن ذلك يفعل ما لم يبلغ به الإمام. فإذا بُلغ به الإمام فلا أعفاه اللّٰه إن أعفاه. رواه ابن أبي شيبة (٢٨٦٥٩). وعن الزبيد بن الصلت قال: سمعت أبا بكر الصديق يقول: لو أخذت شارباً لأحببت أن يستره الله، ولو أخذت سارقاً لأحببت أن يستره الله. رواه ابن أبي شيبة (٢٨٦٦٤).

6736 — Ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Whoever's intercession prevents one of the prescribed punishments (hudud) of Allah from being executed, he has opposed Allah in His command.”
Sahih: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3597), Ahmad (5385), and al-Hakim (2/27). And in it (the narration) it adds: “And whoever dies while owing a debt, it will not be paid with dinars or dirhams, but rather with good deeds and bad deeds. And whoever disputes in a falsehood while he knows it, he remains under the wrath of Allah until he desists. And whoever speaks about a believer that which is not true, Allah will lodge him in the mud of discharge (Radghat al-Khabal) until he retracts what he said.”
His saying: “'Whoever's intercession prevents'” means: whoever has a prescribed punishment of Allah proven against him, and it has reached the ruler. However, before reaching the ruler, or in matters concerning human rights, it is permissible for the judge to intercede; rather, it is recommended for him to do so, even by spending wealth, just as the Prophet ﷺ used to do. It was said to 'Ali, when he interceded for a thief, “Do you intercede for a thief?” He replied, “Yes, that may be done as long as it has not reached the ruler. But if it has reached the ruler, then may Allah not forgive him if he forgives him.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah (28659). And on the authority of al-Zubayd ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq saying, “If I caught a drinker, I would prefer that Allah conceals him, and if I caught a thief, I would prefer that Allah conceals him.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah (28664).

٦٧٣٧ — عن بهز بن حكيم بن معاوية، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: أخذ النبي ﷺ ناسا من قومي في تهمة فحبسهم، فجاء رجلٌ من قومي إلى النبي ﷺ وهو يخطب، فقال: يا محمد علامَ تحبس جيرتي؟ فصمت النبي ﷺ فقال: إن ناسا ليقولون إنك تنهى عن الشر، وتستخلي به! فقال النبي ﷺ: (( ما يقول؟ )) قال: فجعلت أُعرِّض بينهما بالكلام مخافة أن يسمعَها، فيدعوَ على قومي دعوةً لا يفلحون بعدها أبدا، فلم يزل النبي ﷺ به حتى فهِمَها فقال: (( قد قالوها أو قائلُها منهم؟، والله لو فعلت لكان عليَّ وما كان عليهم، خلوا له عن جيرانه)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٣٠)، والترمذي (١٤١٧)، والنسائي (٤٨٧٥)، وأحمد (٢٠٠١٩).

6737 — Bahz ibn Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah narrated on the authority of his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Prophet ﷺ detained some people from my tribe on suspicion and imprisoned them. A man from my tribe came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was delivering a sermon and said, “O Muhammad! On what grounds are you detaining my neighbors?” The Prophet ﷺ remained silent. The man then said, “Some people say that you forbid evil but practice it in private!” The Prophet ﷺ said, “What is he saying?” The narrator said: I began to obscure the words between them, fearing that the Prophet ﷺ would hear it and supplicate against my tribe a supplication from which they would never prosper. But the Prophet ﷺ kept questioning him until he understood it, so he said, “Have they really said it, or is the one saying it from among them? By Allah, if I were to do that, the sin would be upon me and not upon them. Release his neighbors for him.”
Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3630), al-Tirmidhi (1417), al-Nasa'i (4875), and Ahmad (20019).

٦٧٣٨ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: إن أناسا كانوا يؤخذون بالوحي في عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وإن الوحي قد انقطع، وإنما نأخذ الآن بما ظهر لنا من أعمالكم، فمن أظهر لنا خيراً آمنّاه وقرّبناه، وليس لنا من سريرته شيء، اللّٰه يحاسبه في سريرته، ومن أظهر لنا سوءاً لم نأمنه ولم نصدقه، وإن قال: إن سريرته حسنة.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٤١).

6738 — 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: People used to be judged by the revelation during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but now the revelation has ceased. We judge you now only by what is manifest to us of your deeds. Whoever shows us good, we will trust him and bring him close, and we have nothing to do with his inner secrets; Allah will call him to account for his inner secrets. But whoever shows us evil, we will not trust him and we will not believe him, even if he claims that his inner secret is good.
Sahih: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2641).

٦٧٣٨ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: إن أناسا كانوا يؤخذون بالوحي في عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وإن الوحي قد انقطع، وإنما نأخذ الآن بما ظهر لنا من أعمالكم، فمن أظهر لنا خيراً آمنّاه وقرّبناه، وليس لنا من سريرته شيء، اللّٰه يحاسبه في سريرته، ومن أظهر لنا سوءاً لم نأمنه ولم نصدقه، وإن قال: إن سريرته حسنة.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٤١).
6738 — 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: People used to be judged by the revelation during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but now the revelation has ceased. We judge you now only by what is manifest to us of your deeds. Whoever shows us good, we will trust him and bring him close, and we have nothing to do with his inner secrets; Allah will call him to account for his inner secrets. But whoever shows us evil, we will not trust him and we will not believe him, even if he claims that his inner secret is good.
Sahih: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2641).

arabic_source:
٦٧٣٩ — عن أنس قال: مرّ على النبي ﷺ بجنازة فأثنوا عليها خيراً، فقال: (( وجبت )) ثم مُرّ بأخرى فأثنوا عليها شراً - أو قال غير ذلك - فقال: (( وجبت )) فقيل: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قلت لهذا وجبت ولهذا وجبت؟! قال: (( شهادة القوم، المؤمنون شهداء اللّٰه في الأرض)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٤٢)، ومسلم (٩٤٩:٦٠)، والسياق للبخاري.

6739 — Anas said: A funeral procession passed by the Prophet ﷺ and the people praised the deceased. He said, “It has become binding.” Then another procession passed by and they spoke ill of the deceased—or said something else—and he said, “It has become binding.” It was said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, you said 'It has become binding' for this one and 'It has become binding' for that one?!” He said, “It is the testimony of the people; the believers are the witnesses of Allah on earth.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2642) and Muslim (949:60), and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.

٦٧٤٠ — عن عمران بن حصين قال: قال النبي ﷺ: (( خيركم قرني ثم الذين يلونهم، ثم الذين يلونهم )) قال عمران: لا أدري، أذكر النبي ﷺ بعد قرنين أو ثلاثة، قال النبي ﷺ: (( إن بعدكم قوماً يخونون ولا يؤتمنون، ويشهدون ولا يستشهدون، وينذرون ولا يفون، ويظهر فيهم السمن )).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٥١) ومسلم (٢٥٣٥:٢١٤).

6740 — 'Imran ibn Husayn said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The best of you is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them.” 'Imran said: I do not know whether the Prophet ﷺ mentioned two or three generations after his generation. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed, after you there will be a people who will betray and will not be trusted, they will bear witness without being asked to bear witness, they will make vows and not fulfill them, and obesity will appear among them.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2651) and Muslim (2535:214).

٦٧٤١ — عن عبد اللّه بن مسعود، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( خير الناس قرني، ثم الذين يلونهم، ثم الذين يلونهم، ثم يجئ أقوام تسبق شهادة أحدهم يمينه، ويمينه شهادته)) قال إبراهيم: وكانوا يضربوننا على الشهادة والعهد.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٥٢) ومسلم (٢٥٣٣:٢١).

6741 — 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The best of people are those of my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, then there will come people whose testimony will precede their oath, and their oath will precede their testimony.” Ibrahim said: They used to strike us for giving testimony and making covenants (when we were young, to teach us seriousness).
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2652) and Muslim (2533:21).

صحيح: رواه مالك (٣) ومسلم (١٧١٩).

Sahih: Narrated by Malik (3) and Muslim (1719).

حسن: رواه البخاري في التاريخ الكبير (١٠٤٩) وأحمد (٣٩٨٢) والطحاوي في مشكله (١٥٩٠) والحاكم (٤٤٥/٤).

6743 — Ibn Mas'ud narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed, before the Hour there will be the greeting of only those one knows, the widespread expansion of trade, the prevalence of false testimony, and the concealment of the testimony of truth.”
Hasan: Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (1049), Ahmad (3982), al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar (1590), and al-Hakim (4/445).

٦٧٤٦ — عن عائشة قالت في حديث الإفك: فدعا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بريرة، فقال: (( يا بريرة، هل رأيتِ فيها شيئا يريبكِ؟ )) فقالت بريرة: لا والذي بعثك بالحق، إن رأيت منها أمراً أغمصه عليها قط أكثر من أنها جارية حديثة السن، تنام عن العجين، فتأتي الداجن فتأكله. وجاء في آخره: وكان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يسأل زينبَ بنت جحش عن أمري، فقال: (( يا زينبُ، ما علمتِ ما رأيتِ؟ )) فقالت: يا رسول الله ﷺ، أحمي سمعي وبصري، والله ما علمتُ عليها إلا خيراً، قالت (أي عائشة): وهي التي كانت تساميني، فعصمها اللّٰه بالورع.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٦١)، ومسلم (٢٧٧٠).

6746 — 'Aishah said in the narration of the slander (al-Ifk): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Barirah and said, “O Barirah, have you seen anything in her that arouses your suspicion?” Barirah said, “No, by the One Who sent you with the truth, I have never seen any fault in her for which I could blame her, other than that she is a young girl who falls asleep leaving her family's dough, and the domestic goat comes and eats it.” And it states at the end of it: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask Zaynab bint Jahsh about my matter, saying, “O Zaynab, what did you know? What did you see?” She replied, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I protect my hearing and my sight; by Allah, I know nothing of her but good.” 'Aishah said: She was the one who used to compete with me (in status), yet Allah protected her because of her piety.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2661) and Muslim (2770).

arabic_source:
٦٧٤٧ — عن عبد الله بن عمر، عن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أنه قال: (( يا معشر النساء تصدقن وأكثرن الاستغفار، فإني رأيتكن أكثر أهل النار)) فقالت امرأة منهن، جزلة: وما لنا يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أكثر أهل النار؟! قال: (( تكثرن اللعن، وتكفرن العشير، وما رأيت من ناقصات عقل ودين أغلب لذي لبّ منكن)) قالت: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وما نقصان العقل والدين؟ قال: (( أما نقصان العقل فشهادة امرأتين تعدل شهادة رجل، فهذا نقصان العقل، وتمكث الليالي ما تصلي وتُفطر في رمضان، فهذا نقصان الدين)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٧٩).

english_source:
6747 — 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O assembly of women, give charity and seek forgiveness frequently, for I have seen that you form the majority of the people of the Fire.” A wise woman among them said, “Why is it, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that we form the majority of the people of the Fire?” He said, “You curse frequently and you are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen anyone deficient in intelligence and religion more capable of overcoming a wise man than one of you.” She said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what is the deficiency in intelligence and religion?” He said, “As for the deficiency in intelligence, the testimony of two women equals the testimony of one man; this is the deficiency in intelligence. And she spends nights without praying and breaks her fast in Ramadan (due to menses); this is the deficiency in religion.”
Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (79).

6748 — Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Is not the testimony of a woman equal to half the testimony of a man?” We said, “Yes.” He said, “That is due to the deficiency in her intelligence.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2658) and Muslim (80), and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.

٦٧٤٩ — عن عقبة بن الحارث أنه تزوج أم يحيى بنت أبي إهاب، قال: فجاءت أمة سوداء فقالت: قد أرضعتكما، فذكرت ذلك للنبي ﷺ فأعرض عني، قال: فتنحيت فذكرت ذلك له، قال: (( وكيف وقد زعمت أن قد أرضعتكما )) فنهاه عنها. وفي رواية: (( وكيف وقد قيل! دَعْها عنك)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٥٩)، والرواية الأخرى عنده أيضا (٢٦٦٠).

6749 — 'Uqbah ibn al-Harith narrated that he married Umm Yahya bint Abi Ihab. He said: A black slave-girl came and said, “I have breast-fed both of you.” I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, but he turned his face away from me. I moved to face him and mentioned it to him again. He said, “How can you remain with her when she has claimed that she breast-fed both of you?” So he forbade him from remaining with her. And in another narration: “How can you when it has been said! Leave her.”
Sahih: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2659), and the other narration is also with him (2660).

He said, “How can you remain with her when she has claimed that she breast-fed both of you?” So he forbade him from remaining with her. And in another narration: “How can you when it has been said! Leave her.”

٦٧٤٩ — عن عقبة بن الحارث أنه تزوج أم يحيى بنت أبي إهاب، قال: فجاءت أمة سوداء فقالت: قد أرضعتكما، فذكرت ذلك للنبي ﷺ فأعرض عني، قال: فتنحيت فذكرت ذلك له، قال: (( وكيف وقد زعمت أن قد أرضعتكما )) فنهاه عنها. وفي رواية: (( وكيف وقد قيل! دَعْها عنك)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٥٩)، والرواية الأخرى عنده أيضا (٢٦٦٠).

٦٧٥٠ — عن عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللهِ بْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ أَنَّ بَنِي صُهَيْبٍ مَوْلَى ابْنِ جُدْعَانَ ادَّعَوْا بَيْتَيْنِ وَحُجْرَةً أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللٰهِ أَعْطَى ذَلِكَ صُهَيْبًا، فَقَالَ مَرْوَانُ: مَنْ يَشْهَدُ لَكُمَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ؟ قَالُوا: ابْنُ عُمَرَ. فَدَعَاهُ، فَشَهِدَ لَأَعْطَى رَسُولُ اللٰهِ ﷺ صُهَيْبًا بَيْتَيْنِ وَحُجْرَةً، فَقَضَى مَرْوَانُ بِشَهَادَتِهِ لَهُمْ.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٢٤).

6750 — 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated that the sons of Suhayb, the freed slave of Ibn Jud'an, claimed two houses and a room, stating that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given that to Suhayb. Marwan asked, “Who will bear witness for you to that effect?” They said, “Ibn 'Umar.” So Marwan called him, and he bore witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had indeed given Suhayb two houses and a room. Marwan then passed judgment in their favor based on his testimony.
Sahih: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2624).

٦٧٥١ — عن النعمان بن بشير قال: سألت أمي أبي بعض الموهبة لي من ماله، ثم بدا له فوهبها لي، فقالت: لا أرضى حتى تشهد النبي ﷺ فأخذ بيدي وأنا غلام، فأتى بي النبي ﷺ فقال: إن أمه بنت رواحة سألتني بعض الموهبة لهذا؟ قال: (( ألك ولد سواه؟ )) قال: نعم. قال: فأراه قال: (( لا تُشهدني على جور )).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٥٠)، ومسلم (١٦٢٣:١٤).

6751 — Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir said: My mother asked my father to grant me a gift from his wealth, then it occurred to him and he gifted it to me. She said, “I will not be pleased until you take the Prophet ﷺ as a witness.” So he took me by my hand while I was a young boy, and brought me to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “His mother, the daughter of Rawahah, asked me to grant a gift to this boy.” The Prophet ﷺ asked, “Do you have any children other than him?” He replied, “Yes.” He said, and I think he said: “Do not make me a witness to an injustice.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2650) and Muslim (1623:14).

٦٧٥٢ — عن عروة بن الزبير: أن امرأة سرقت في غزوة الفتح، فأتي بها رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ثم أمر فقطعت يدها. قالت عائشة: فحسنت توبتها وتزوّجت، وكانت تأتي بعد ذلك فأرفع حاجتها إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٤٨) ومسلم (١٦٨٨:٩) والسياق للبخاري.

6752 — 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated that a woman committed theft during the expedition of the Conquest (of Makkah). She was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who ordered that her hand be amputated. 'Aishah said: Her repentance became excellent afterward and she married, and she used to come to me after that so that I could convey her needs to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2648) and Muslim (1688:9), and the wording is that of al-Bukhari.

٦٧٥٣ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ رد شهادة الخائن والخائنة، وذي الغِمرة على أخيه، ورد شهادة القانع لأهل البيت، وأجازها لغيرهم.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٠٠)، وأحمد (٦٨٩٨)، والدارقطني (٢٤٣/٤)، والبيهقي (٢٠٠/١٠).
قال أبو داود: الغِمْر: الحِنَة والشحناء، والقانع: الأجير التابع مثل الأجير الخاص.

english_source:
6753 — Amr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejected the testimony of a dishonest man and a dishonest woman, and of a person bearing rancor against his brother, and he rejected the testimony of a dependent servant for the household, while allowing it for others.
Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3600), Ahmad (6898), al-Daraqutni (4/243), and al-Bayhaqi (10/200).
Abu Dawud said: al-ghimr means malice and enmity. Al-qaniʿ means the dependent hired servant, such as a personal servant.

حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٠٠)، وأحمد (٦٨٩٨)، والدارقطني (٢٤٣/٤)، والبيهقي (٢٠٠/١٠).
قال أبو داود: الغِمْر: الحِنَة والشحناء، والقانع: الأجير التابع مثل الأجير الخاص.
6753 — Amr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejected the testimony of a dishonest man and a dishonest woman, and of a person bearing rancor against his brother, and he rejected the testimony of a dependent servant for the household, while allowing it for others.
Hasan: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3600), Ahmad (6898), al-Daraqutni (4/243), and al-Bayhaqi (10/200).
Abu Dawud said: al-ghimr means malice and enmity. Al-qaniʿ means the dependent hired servant, such as a personal servant.

٦٧٥٤ — عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( من حلف على يمين- وهو فيها فاجر - ليقتطع بها مال امرئ مسلم لقي اللّٰه وهو عليه غضبان )) قال: فقال الأشعث بن قيس فيّ والله كان ذلك، كان بيني وبين رجل من اليهود أرض فجحدني، فقدّمته إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال لي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
 (( ألك بيّنة؟ )) قلت: لا، قال: فقال لليهودي: احلف. قال: قلت: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إذن يحلف ويذهب بمالي. قال: فأنزل اللّٰه تعالى: ( إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ ثَمَنَا قَلِيلًا) إلى آخر الآية.
 [آل عمران: ٧٧ ] وفي رواية: (( شاهداك أو يمينه ).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٦٦٦،٢٦٦٧) ومسلم (٢٢٠ :١٣٨).
 والرواية الأخرى عند البخاري (٢٦٦٩،٢٦٧٠) ومسلم (٢٢١:١٣٨).

6754 — Ibn Masʿud reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever swears an oath while lying in it in order to unlawfully take the wealth of a Muslim will meet Allah while He is angry with him.”
 Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said: By Allah, this was about me. There was a dispute between me and a Jewish man concerning land, and he denied my claim. So I brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Do you have proof?” I said: No. He then said to the Jew: “Swear an oath.” I said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he will swear and take my property. Then Allah revealed: “Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price…” to the end of the verse [Aal Imran: 77].
 In another narration: “Your two witnesses, or else his oath.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (2666, 2667) and Muslim (220:138).
 The other wording is in al-Bukhari (2669, 2670) and Muslim (221:138).

٦٧٥٥ — عن وائل بن حجر قال: جاء رجل من حضرموت ورجل من كندة إلى النبي ﷺ فقال الحضرمي: يا رسول الله ﷺ، إن هذا قد غلبني على أرض كانت لأبي. فقال الكندي: هي أرضي في يدي أزرعها ليس له فيها حق. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ للحضرمي: (( ألك بينة؟ )) قال: لا. قال: (( فلك بيمينه )) قال: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إن الرجل فاجر لا يبالي على ما حلف عليه، وليس يتورّع من شيء. فقال:
 (( ليس لك منه إلا ذلك ))، فانطلق ليحلف، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لما أدبر: (( أما لئن حلف على ماله ليأكله ظلماً، ليلقين اللّٰه وهو عنه مُعْرِض )).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٣:١٣٩).

6755 — Waʾil ibn Hujr said: A man from Hadramawt and a man from Kindah came to the Prophet ﷺ. The Hadrami said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this man has seized land that belonged to my father. The Kindi said: It is my land, in my possession, and I cultivate it; he has no right to it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Hadrami: “Do you have proof?” He said: No. He said: “Then you are entitled to his oath.” He said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the man is wicked; he does not care what he swears upon and he refrains from nothing. He said: “You have no right against him except that.”
 So the man went off to swear, and when he turned away the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If he swears to seize his property unjustly, he will surely meet Allah while Allah is turned away from him.”
 Sahih: Narrated by Muslim (223:139).

arabic_source:
٦٧٥٦ — عن أبي موسى قال: اختصم رجلان إلى النبي ﷺ في أرض، أحدهما من
 أهل حضرموت. قال: فجعل يمين أحدهما، قال: فضج الآخر، وقال: إنه إذا يذهب بأرضي، فقال:
 (( إن هو اقتطعها بيمينه ظلماً، كان ممن لا ينظر اللّٰه عز وجل إليه يوم القيامة، ولا يزكيه، وله عذاب أليم)) قال: وورع الآخر فردّها.
 صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٩٥١٤) والبزار -كشف الأستار (١٣٥٩) وأبو يعلى (٧٢٧٤).

6756 — Abu Musa said: Two men brought a dispute over land to the Prophet ﷺ, one of them being from Hadramawt. He ruled that one of them should swear an oath. The other cried out and said: Then he will take my land! He said: “If he takes it by his oath unjustly, he will be among those at whom Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify him, and he will have a painful punishment.” The other man then refrained and returned it.
 Sahih: Narrated by Ahmad (19514), al-Bazzar in Kashf al-Astar (1359), and Abu Yaʿla (7274).

أن امرأتين كانتا تخرزان في بيت - أو في الحجرة - فخرجت إحداهما وقد أُنفذ بإشفى في كفها، فادعت على الأخرى، فرفع إلى ابن عباس.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٥٥٢)، ومسلم (١٧١١/١)، والسياق للبخاري.

6757 — Ibn Abī Mulaykah reported:
Two women were sewing leather in a house—or in a room—when one of them came out with an awl driven into the palm of her hand. She accused the other woman, and the matter was brought before Ibn ʿAbbās.
Ibn ʿAbbās said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“If people were granted what they claimed merely on the basis of their claims, the blood and wealth of people would be lost.”
He said:
“Remind her of Allah and recite to her:
‘Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah…’”
 [Āl ʿImrān: 77]
They reminded her, and she confessed.
Then Ibn ʿAbbās said that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4552) and Muslim (1711/1). This is the wording of al-Bukhārī. 
The word ishfā means the pointed iron tool used for piercing leather while sewing.

 Sahih: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3616), Ibn Majah (2329), Ahmad (10347), and al-Daraqutni (4/211).

٦٧٦٨ — عن عمارة بن خزيمة أن عمه حدّثه - وهو من أصحاب النبي ﷺ - أن النبي ﷺ ابتاع فرساً من أعرابي، فاستتبعه النبي ﷺ ليقضيه ثمن فرسه، فأسرع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ المشي وأبطأ الأعرابي، فطفق رجال يعترضون الأعرابي فيساومونه بالفرس، ولا يشعرون أن النبي ﷺ ابتاعه، فنادى الأعرابي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: إن كنت مبتاعاً هذا الفرس وإلا بعته. فقام النبي ﷺ حين سمع نداء الأعرابي فقال: (( أوليس قد ابتعته منك؟ )) فقال الأعرابي: لا، والله ما بعتكه. فقال النبي ﷺ: (( بلى، قد ابتعته منك )). فطفق الأعرابي يقول: هلم شهيداً. فقال خزيمة بن ثابت: أنا أشهد أنك قد بايعته. فأقبل النبي ﷺ على خزيمة فقال: (( بم تشهد؟ )) فقال: بتصديقك يا رسول الله ﷺ. فجعل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ شهادة خزيمة بشهادة رجلين.
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٠٧)، والنسائي (٤٦٤٧)، وأحمد (٢١٨٨٣)، والحاكم (١٧-١٨/٢).

6768 — Umarah ibn Khuzaymah reported that his uncle—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—said that the Prophet ﷺ bought a horse from a Bedouin. Then the Prophet ﷺ asked him to follow so he could pay him the price of the horse. The Prophet ﷺ walked quickly while the Bedouin lagged behind. Men began approaching the Bedouin and bargaining with him over the horse, not realizing that the Prophet ﷺ had already bought it. The Bedouin then called out to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: If you are buying this horse, then buy it, otherwise I will sell it. When the Prophet ﷺ heard the call of the Bedouin, he stood and said: “Have I not already bought it from you?” The Bedouin said: No, by Allah, I have not sold it to you. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Rather, I have bought it from you.” The Bedouin then kept saying: Bring a witness. Khuzaymah ibn Thabit said: I testify that you did indeed make the sale with him.
 The Prophet ﷺ turned to Khuzaymah and said: “On what basis do you testify?” He said: By believing you, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Prophet ﷺ made the testimony of Khuzaymah equal to the testimony of two men.
 Sahih: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3607), al-Nasa’i (4647), Ahmad (21883), and al-Hakim (2/17–18).

٦٧٦٩ — عن ابن عباس قال: خرج رجل من بني سَهُم مع تميم الداري وعدي بن بداء. فمات السهمي بأرض ليس بها مسلم. فلما قدما بتركته فقدوا جاماً من فضة مخوّصا بالذهب. فأحلفهما رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم وجدوا الجام بمكة، فقيل: اشتريناه من عدي وتميم، فقام رجلان من أولياء السهمي، فحلفا بالله: لشهادتنا أحق من شهادتهما. وإن الجام لصاحبهم. قال: وفيهم نزلت: (يَأْيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا شَهَٰدَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَأَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ حِينَ ٱلْوَصِيَّةِ ٱثْنَانِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ أَوْ ءَاخَرَانٍ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ) [ المائدة: ١٠٦ ]
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٨٠).

٦٧٧٠ — عن الشعبي:
أن رجلًا من المسلمين حضرته الوفاة بدقوقاء هذه، ولم يجد أحدًا من المسلمين يشهده على وصيته، فأشهد رجلين من أهل الكتاب.
فقدما الكوفة، فأتيا أبا موسى الأشعري فأخبراه، وقدما بتركته ووصيته.
فقال الأشعري:
هذا أمر لم يكن بعد الذي كان في عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فأحلفهما بعد العصر بالله ما خانا، ولا كذبا، ولا بدلا، ولا كتما، ولا غيرا، وإنها لوصية الرجل وتركته.
فأمضى شهادتهما.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٠٥)، والبيهقي (١٠/١٦٥). 
ودقوقاء - بفتح الدال المهملة، وضم القاف، وبالقاف المقصورة - وهي بلد بين بغداد وإربل.

6770 — Al-Shaʿbī reported:
A Muslim man was near death in Daqūqāʾ and could not find any Muslims to witness his will, so he called two men from the People of the Book as witnesses.
They later came to Kūfah and went to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī. They informed him of what had happened and brought with them the man’s estate and his will.
Al-Ashʿarī said:
“This is a matter that has not occurred since the case that occurred during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
After the ʿAṣr prayer, he made the two men swear by Allah that they had neither betrayed the trust, lied, altered anything, concealed anything, nor changed anything, and that this was truly the man’s will and estate.
He then accepted their testimony.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3605) and al-Bayhaqī (10/165). 
Daqūqāʾ is a town situated between Baghdad and Irbil.

٦٧٧٢ — عن أبي هريرة أن النبي ﷺ قال: (( إذا اختلفتم في الطريق جُعل عرضه سبع أذرع)).
 متفق عليه: رواه مسلم (١٦١٣)، والبخاري (٢٤٧٣) ولفظه: قضى النبي ﷺ إذا تشاجروا في الطريق سبعة أذرع.

6772 — Abu Hurairah reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “If you dispute concerning the road, its width is to be made seven cubits.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by Muslim (1613), and al-Bukhari (2473), whose wording is: The Prophet ﷺ ruled, when they disputed over a road, that it should be seven cubits.

6773 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reported:
Two men brought a dispute before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the protected surrounding space of a date palm.
He ordered that it be measured, and it was found to be seven cubits.
In another narration: five cubits.
He then gave judgment accordingly.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3640).

٦٧٧٤ — عن عمير مولى آبي اللحم قال: أقبلت مع سادتي نريد الهجرة حتى إذا دنونا من المدينة، قال: فدخلوا المدينة وخلفوني في ظهورهم، قال: فأصابني مجاعة شديدة، قال: فمر بي بعض من يخرج من المدينة، فقالوا لي: لو دخلت المدينة، فأصبت من ثمر حوائطها، فدخلت حائطاً فقطعت منه قنوين، فأتاني صاحب الحائط، فأتى بي إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وأخبره خبري، وعليَّ ثوبان، فقال لي: ((أيهما أفضل؟)) فأشرت له إلى أحدهما، فقال: ((خذه))، وأعطى صاحب الحائط الآخر، وخلى سبيلي.
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (٢١٩٤٢).

6774 — ʿUmayr, the freedman of Abi al-Lahm, said: I came with my masters intending hijrah, and when we drew near to Madinah, they entered the city and left me behind with their baggage. Then severe hunger struck me. Some people passing by me on their way out of Madinah said to me: “If you entered Madinah, you could get some fruit from its orchards.” So I entered an orchard and cut two clusters from it. Then the owner of the orchard came, took me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and informed him of my case. I had two garments on me. He said to me: “Which of them is better?” I pointed to one of them, so he said: “Take it,” and he gave the other one to the owner of the orchard and let me go.
 Hasan: Narrated by Imam Ahmad (21942).

arabic_source:
٦٧٧٥ — عن عبد الله بن الزبير:
أن رجلًا من الأنصار خاصم الزبير عند رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في شراج الحرة التي يسقون بها النخل.
فقال الأنصاري:
سرح الماء يمر.
فأبى عليه، فاختصما إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ للزبير:
«اسْقِ يَا زُبَيْرُ، ثُمَّ أَرْسِلِ الْمَاءَ إِلَى جَارِكَ».
فغضب الأنصاري فقال:
أن كان ابن عمتك؟
فتلون وجه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ثم قال:
«اسْقِ يَا زُبَيْرُ، ثُمَّ احْبِسِ الْمَاءَ حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَى الْجَدْرِ».
فقال الزبير:
والله إني لأحسب هذه الآية نزلت في ذلك:
﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾
 [النساء: ٦٥]
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٢٣٥٩)، ومسلم (٢٣٥٧).

6775 — ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr reported:
A man from the Anṣār disputed with al-Zubayr before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning the water channels of al-Ḥarrah by which they irrigated their date palms.
The Anṣārī said:
“Let the water flow onward.”
Al-Zubayr refused, so they brought their dispute before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-Zubayr:
“Water your land, O Zubayr, then release the water to your neighbor.”
The Anṣārī became angry and said:
“Is it because he is your maternal aunt’s son?”
The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed color. He then said:
“Water your land, O Zubayr, then retain the water until it reaches the wall.”
Al-Zubayr said:
“By Allah, I believe this verse was revealed concerning that:
‘But no, by your Lord, they will not truly believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves.’”
 [al-Nisāʾ: 65]
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2359) and Muslim (2357).

٦٧٧٦ — عن ثعلبة بن أبي مالك أنه سمع كبراءهم يذكرون أن رجلاً من قريش كان له سهم في بني قريظة، فخاصم إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في مهزور - يعني السيل الذي يقتسمون ماءه. فقضى بينهم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن الماء إلى الكعبين، ولا يحبس الأعلى على الأسفل.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٣٨)، وابن ماجه (٢٤٨١).

6776 — Tha‘labah ibn Abi Malik reported that he heard their elders mention that a man from Quraysh had a share among Banu Qurayzah, and he brought a dispute before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding Mahzur — meaning the floodwater whose water they divided among themselves. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged between them that the water should be kept up to the ankles, and that the upper landowner should not hold it back from the lower one beyond that.
 Hasan: narrated by Abu Dawud (3638) and Ibn Majah (2481).

٦٧٧٧ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قضى في سيل مهزور أن يُمسك حتى يبلغ الكعبين، ثم يرسل الماء.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٣٩) وابن ماجه (٢٤٨٢).
6777 — ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged concerning the floodwater of Mahzur that it should be held until it reached the ankles, then the water should be released.
 Hasan: narrated by Abu Dawud (3639) and Ibn Majah (2482).

٦٧٧٨ — عن أنس أن النبي ﷺ كان عند بعض نسائه، فأرسلت إحدى أمهات المؤمنين مع خادم بقصعة فيها طعام، فضربت بيدها فكسرت القصعة، فضمها وجعل فيها الطعام. وقال: ((كلوا)). وحبس الرسولَ والقصعة حتى فرغوا. فدفع القصعة الصحيحة، وحبس المكسورة.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٤٨١) و (٥٢٢٥).

6778 — Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ was with one of his wives, and one of the Mothers of the Believers sent, through a servant, a bowl containing food. The wife who was with him struck it with her hand and broke the bowl. He gathered its pieces together and placed the food in it, then said: “Eat.” He kept the servant and the bowl until they had finished, then he gave the sound bowl and kept the broken one.
 Sahih: narrated by al-Bukhari (2481) and (5225).

٦٧٧٩ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: (( لا يمنع أحدكم جاره خشبة يغرزها في جداره)). ثم يقول أبو هريرة: مالي أراكم عنها معرضين، والله لأرمين بها بين أكتافكم.
 متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٣٤) والبخاري (٢٤٦٣) ومسلم (١٦٠٩).

6779 — Abu Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you should prevent his neighbor from placing a piece of wood into his wall.” Then Abu Hurayrah would say: “Why do I see you turning away from this? By Allah, I will surely cast it between your shoulders.”
 Agreed upon: narrated by Malik (34), al-Bukhari (2463), and Muslim (1609).

arabic_source:
٦٧٨٠ — عن ابن عباس: أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال:
«لَا يَمْنَعْ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ مَرْفِقَهُ أَنْ يَضَعَ عَلَى جِدَارِهِ».
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٠٧)، وابن ماجه (٢٣٣٧).
ولفظ ابن ماجه:
«لَا يَمْنَعْ أَحَدُكُمْ جَارَهُ أَنْ يَغْرِزَ خَشَبَةً عَلَى جِدَارِهِ».
وقوله: «المرفق» هو كل ما يُرتفق به، أي يُنتفع به.

english_source:
6780 — Ibn ʿAbbās reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“None of you should prevent his brother from making use of his wall for something from which he may benefit.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (2307) and Ibn Mājah (2337).
The wording of Ibn Mājah is:
“None of you should prevent his neighbor from placing a piece of wood upon his wall.”
The word al-mirfaq refers to anything by which benefit or practical use is obtained.
